earliest_valid_point_in_time_tape_date_r.claim_under_test: MARKET_PROGRAM_RESPONSE_2026-08-06.md section 1: 'Genuine point-in-time capture exists only from 2026-07-31 onward -- our own daily jobs.' Section 2: 'Point-in-time capture, live since 2026-07-31 (D11_LIVE_INFORMATION_CAPTURE, PASSED).'
earliest_valid_point_in_time_tape_date_r.ruling: FALSIFIED AS STATED, for three of the four owned capture streams examined. Bytes show first-seen (witnessed, T0) timestamps as follows: odds capture (S1) 2026-07-30T15:01:32Z; injury capture (S4) 2026-07-30T15:49:50Z; news capture (S5) 2026-07-30T16:25:50Z; referee capture (S6) 2026-07-30T17:08:06Z. Only props capture (S2) actually starts 2026-07-31T14:23:41Z, one day later than the other four streams. The earliest valid point-in-time tape date across all owned T0 capture streams is therefore 2026-07-30, not 2026-07-31.
earliest_valid_point_in_time_tape_date_r.method: Read the producing script for each stream to confirm the timestamp field is our own retrieval-time write (T0 semantics), then took min(first-seen timestamp) per stream via Import-Csv / directory listing against the live main worktree's data/ files.
earliest_valid_point_in_time_tape_date_r.caveat: This ruling is about the EARLIEST WITNESSED CAPTURE date across the owned T0 streams, not about the earliest date any market-relevant table in the repository references. The T2 final-state archive (S7/S8) covers dates back to 2022-05-21 and the T1 props-historical backfill (S3) covers dates back to 2024-05-14, but neither is a witnessed point-in-time record -- both are excluded from this ruling by definition (TAXONOMY.json point_in_time_integrity rule 1: 'requires a capture record whose first-seen (witnessed) timestamp is at or before T, of tier T0 (or T1 under tier rules)'; the ruling here is specifically about T0 witness, the strongest tier).
